item.title: Tailevu finds a taste of home in Taveuni ahead of Skipper Cup clash
item.description: Tailevu may be hundreds of kilometres away from home, but the players have been reminded that support for the team extends beyond provincial boundaries after members of the Tailevu community living in Taveuni visited them in camp. The Tailevu rugby team is currently in camp at Wairiki as they prepare for their Skipper Cup clash against Taveuni tomorrow.
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu may be hundreds of kilometres away from home, but the players have been reminded that support for the team extends beyond provincial boundaries after members of the Tailevu community living in Taveuni visited them in camp.

The Tailevu rugby team is currently in camp at Wairiki as they prepare for their Skipper Cup clash against Taveuni tomorrow.

People with connections to Tailevu through their parents, grandparents, marriage or vasu ties visited the players, bringing a little piece of home to the team.

Members of the Nadroga-Navosa community living in Taveuni, along with traditional leaders and women from Taveuni, also joined the gathering.

The team says the visit showed that the bonds of the vanua extend beyond rugby and the jersey, with people continuing to support the players even when they are far from home.

They also thanked the Dra VakaTailevu community residing in Nayavu and Wairiki, as well as Nadroga-Navosa Taveuni, for their support.

The team also acknowledged Merridian Store and the Niumataiwalu family from Dre’eti, Qamea, for their contributions.

Tailevu says the support has helped the players remain grounded and united as they continue preparations for this weekend's match.

Tailevu is currently third on the Skipper Cup points table with 38 points, while Taveuni is seventh with 25 points.

Nadi moved to the top of the table following their 27-23 victory last Saturday.

Tailevu will take on Taveuni at the Wairiki School Grounds this Saturday.

item.content:encoded:
However, he says every team is working under the same rules and the Bati will have to make the most of the time available.

Potter says the mood in camp is positive, with players spending time together and getting to know each other better.

He says building that connection will be crucial, particularly with several players new to this level of international rugby league.

Potter says while there is plenty of talent in the squad, the Bati will need something special as a team if they are to compete against the world's best.

Meanwhile, Potter says there are no major injury concerns among the players selected for the World Cup.

He says a few players were unavailable for selection because of injuries and post-season operations, including Jahream Bula, who required shoulder surgery.

The Fiji Bati and Fiji Bulikula presented their traditional iTatau to Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru as they prepare to leave for the World Cup.

The Rugby League World Cup kicks off next Thursday, with Australia taking on New Zealand at 9.05pm.

The Bati will begin their campaign against the Cook Islands at 5.05pm next Sunday at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle.

They will then face Australia at 9.05pm on the 25th before taking on New Zealand at 4.30pm on the 31st.

item.title: Fiji 7s stars featured in new Coca-Cola collectible campaign
item.description: Fiji 7s stars Iowane Teba, Rauto Vakadranu, Filipe Sauturaga, Vuiviawa Naduvalo and Joseva Talacolo are being featured in a new collectible campaign celebrating the moments the national team has created for the country. From October 2nd to November 30th, the players will feature on Coca-Cola Classic and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar 330ml cans, 600ml bottles and 2.25-litre bottles.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji 7s stars Iowane Teba, Rauto Vakadranu, Filipe Sauturaga, Vuiviawa Naduvalo and Joseva Talacolo are being featured in a new collectible campaign celebrating the moments the national team has created for the country.

From October 2nd to November 30th, the players will feature on Coca-Cola Classic and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar 330ml cans, 600ml bottles and 2.25-litre bottles.

Speaking at the launch of the Coca Cola x FRU Rugby 7s collectible campaign at Albert Park, Suva, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners Fiji Country Director Pacific Islands Ryan Mahoney says the campaign is about building awareness and celebrating the special moments Fiji 7s has brought to the country.

Mahoney says the campaign gives Fijians an opportunity to relive proud moments created by the national 7s teams, including Olympic gold medal victories.

He says Coca-Cola’s partnership with the Fiji Rugby Union extends from grassroots rugby through to the senior men’s and women’s teams.

Mahoney says rugby remains an all-encompassing sport in Fiji, with the country coming to a standstill whenever the national teams take the field.

Meanwhile, Fiji Rugby Union Director Commercial Tevita Tuiloa says the campaign will allow children across Fiji to see their heroes and be inspired to dream of representing the country.

Tuiloa says featuring the players on products that reach households across Fiji provides a platform to promote the national 7s team.

He says players such as Talacolo once had the same dream of representing Fiji, and their images can now inspire the next generation to believe those dreams are possible.

The Fiji Men’s 7s team finished second in the 2025/2026 SVNS World Series and sixth in the SVNS World Championship.
